chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about the man who is eaten by predatory wild animals and birds, so his bones remain without flesh; how should he be dealt with? He said: He is washed, enshrouded, Salat is prayed over him, and he is buried. And if the deceased is in two halves, Salat is prayed over the half in which is the heart.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ritual ruling for a body eaten by animals where only bones remain?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of *Salat al-Mayyit* for those whose bodies are partially consumed, establishing that the presence of the heart is the decisive criterion for determining the 'half' to be prayed over. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the heart as the central locus of the soul and identity, ensuring the deceased receives full ritual honors even when the body is fragmented. This ruling provides practical guidance for burial in cases of war or natural disasters where complete bodies are not recovered.
